title: Bull Shows Intel Xeon Diamond Rapids Package at SC26
gist: At SC26, Bull's liquid-cooled Sequana XH31600 blade was the only system showing actual Intel Xeon Diamond Rapids packages (LGA9324, 16-channel memory, dual-socket nodes), alongside Bull's BXI interconnect and an NVIDIA ConnectX-8 SuperNIC. ServeTheHome sees Diamond Rapids in sampling with a best-guess Q2 2027 launch, slipping to early September 2027 if June is missed, and notes bespoke HPC blades now compete with high-volume ORv3/AI rack standards.

insights.claim: Intel's Xeon Diamond Rapids server CPU appears to be in the sampling phase as of SC26 (November 2026), with Intel doing something like a mini launch at the show.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Sampling status sets the clock on Intel's next server refresh cycle and OEM revenue timing.
insights.quote: Diamond Rapids seems to be in the sampling phase.
insights.locator: Many other vendors are showing off

insights.claim: ServeTheHome's best guess is that Intel's Xeon Diamond Rapids launches around Q2 2027; if it slips past June, or becomes a split launch of 1P and 2P platforms, the next real launch window is early September 2027.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: A slip past June 2027 pushes Intel's server ramp into H2 2027, extending AMD's window; watch for 1P/2P split-launch signals.
insights.quote: The best guess is maybe we start to see a launch in Q2 2027, but if that slips past June (or it becomes a split launch with 1P platforms and 2P platforms), the next real launch window for Intel is early September 2027.
insights.locator: Many other vendors are showing off

insights.claim: Among the many vendors showing Diamond Rapids systems at SC26, Bull was the only one ServeTheHome found displaying an actual Diamond Rapids CPU package; other vendors showed designs including 32 DIMM per socket 2DPC memory configurations.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Broad OEM platform readiness ahead of launch suggests the ecosystem is preparing for a real ramp.
insights.quote: For its part, Bull is the only one we have found that has a package.
insights.locator: Many other vendors are showing off

insights.claim: The Bull Sequana XH31600 compute blade carries two dual-socket Intel Diamond Rapids nodes (four CPU packages), each node with 16-channel memory, using the LGA9324 socket previously seen on the ASRock Rack DMRD16-2L+ at OCP Summit 2026.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: 16-channel memory and a huge LGA9324 socket signal a step-up in memory bandwidth and board area per CPU, which drives DRAM content per server.
insights.quote: these are two dual-socket compute nodes with Intel Diamond Rapids, each with 16-channel memory.
insights.locator: Just ot be clear about what

insights.claim: Diamond Rapids memory layouts force CPUs onto fairly wide motherboards because of the memory placed on either side of each socket.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Wider boards and more DIMMs per socket raise density/cooling challenges and memory content per node.
insights.quote: the CPUs are on fairly wide motherboards because of all of the memory on either side.
insights.locator: You can see that in the

insights.claim: Bull showed its proprietary BXI interconnect with a 51.2T switch of 64x 800G OSFP ports, but its BXI NICs are QSFP-DD on PCIe Gen5 x16, apparently using two Gen5 x16 links to reach 800Gbps similar to the NVIDIA ConnectX-8 C8240 approach.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Shows how vendors bridge to 800G before PCIe Gen6 NICs are widely available.
insights.quote: Bull showed a BXI switch with 64x 800G OSFP ports, but the BXI NICs were shown as QSFP-DD and PCIe Gen5 x16.

insights.claim: Bull's platform pairs its own PCIe Gen5 BXI NIC with a PCIe Gen6-capable Diamond Rapids CPU, while an NVIDIA ConnectX-8 SuperNIC in OCP NIC 3.0 form factor, a high-volume PCIe Gen6 NIC, sat right next to it as a competitor.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Even sovereign/HPC vendors with in-house fabrics are offering NVIDIA networking, highlighting NVIDIA's encroachment into HPC interconnect.
insights.quote: It’s interesting that Bull has its own interconnect, with a 51.2T switch and a PCIe Gen5 NIC in a platform with a Gen6 CPU, but right next to it is NVIDIA’s high-volume PCIe Gen6 NIC competitor.
insights.locator: What stood out a bit is

themes.theme: Bespoke HPC blades vs high-volume rack standards

insights.claim: The Bull Sequana XH31600 is an incredibly bespoke, fully liquid-cooled blade with blind-mate power and liquid at the rear, heatpipes and liquid cooling blocks on components, and no copper-cabled backplane in the rear.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Full liquid cooling is now table stakes in high-density compute; watch liquid-cooling supply chains.
insights.quote: What is very cool about this platform is that it is incredibly bespoke.
insights.locator: What is very cool about this

insights.claim: With NVIDIA pushing ORv3 and AMD now pushing a double-wide rack, a high-volume industry standard for high-density racks has emerged for power and cooling, raising questions about the future of bespoke designs like Bull's.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Standardization around NVIDIA/AMD rack designs pressures niche HPC system vendors' differentiation and favors high-volume ODM supply chains.
insights.quote: It feels like there is a high-volume standard for high-density racks in the industry if you want power and cooling.
insights.locator: For years, Bull has had one

insights.claim: Platforms like Bull's that would have been mind-blowing years ago now merely fit in alongside higher-volume AI infrastructure such as NVIDIA Vera Rubin designs in ORv3 racks.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: AI infrastructure volume has overtaken HPC as the driver of datacenter hardware innovation.
insights.quote: this type of platform would have been mind-blowing years ago.
insights.locator: What has been interesting at SC26

insights.claim: Bull's differentiator is multi-architecture breadth: it displayed SiPearl, Intel Xeon Diamond Rapids, NVIDIA, and AMD Venice nodes in a common form factor.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Vendor-agnostic platforms (including European SiPearl) appeal to sovereign HPC buyers; AMD Venice and Diamond Rapids compete for the same slots.
insights.quote: What Bull has, however, is SiPearl, Intel Xeon Diamond Rapids, NVIDIA, and AMD Venice nodes on display in a common form factor.
insights.locator: What has been interesting at SC26
